Roblox claims to have made changes to its popular children's app to protect children from predators, but regulators say these protections are not enough.

The regulator identified four significant shortcomings, including that adults can send friend requests to children without parental approval...

Australia's eSafety Commissioner today published the vulnerabilities found during testing:

  • Adults can send friend requests to young Australian children without parental or guardian consent;
  • Children and adults can view and respond to each other's posts on forums outside the game environment without parental or guardian consent;
  • A child's contact list is visible to anyone on the Roblox platform;
  • A child's profile and bio, including non-sensitive personal profile information such as account name, number and names of contacts, avatar image, and interests, are visible to anyone on the Roblox platform, and there is no way to restrict who can see this information

The regulator said Roblox has agreed to implement stricter measures within three months:

  • Prevent adults from contacting unknown children without parental consent
  • Strengthen child account settings so they are set to private mode by default
  • Provide easy-to-use reporting mechanisms and notify users of complaint outcomes
  • Engage an independent third-party auditor to evaluate the effectiveness of its safety measures, including the deployment of age estimation measures

Roblox has more than 380 million active users, the majority of whom are under 16.
